citations.narrative:
Ten dogs were shipped prior to receiving a health certificate. Shipping dogs without having a completed health certificate
doesn't ensure the dogs being shipped are in good health. All dogs being shipped must have a health certificate
completed by a licensed veterinarian no more than 10 days prior to the delivery of the dogs.

Three puppies born on 7/10/25 were shipped on 9/3/25. The puppies would have been 55 days old on the day of sale
which is one das shy of the required 8 weeks of age that they are required to be before being transported. Dogs younger
than 8 weeks of age are more susceptible to stresses that occur from travelling and being placed into a new facility. Their
immune systems are more susceptible to becoming comprised which could cause them to become sick and even die. The
licensee must not ship any puppies under 8 weeks of age unless it is directly to the end consumer.

While reviewing the paperwork, the licensee's young sons had four nursing puppies out of their enclosure and were
playing with them on a chair. One of the puppies fell off the chair and verbalized (squealed out) in pain/discomfort. The
licensee was able to calm that puppy down and the puppy was uninjured. Not handling the puppies carefully and
appropriately can result in trauma, discomfort, or injury to the puppies. The licensee must ensure anyone he authorizes to
handle his dogs/puppies are doing so in a manner as expeditiously and carefully as possible and doesn't cause any
trauma, behavioral stress, physical harm, or unnecessary discomfort to the animals being handled.

None of the adult dogs are vaccinated against distemper or parvo. Not having all the adult dogs current on their
distemper/parvo vaccines doesn't ensure the population is adequately protected against those diseases. All adult dogs
must be vaccinated against distemper and parvo.
This is a 1st Re-License Inspection for a Class "A” license. The inspection and exit briefing were conducted with the
applicant.
All items must be in compliance within 2 more inspections or by August 7th, 2026 or the applicant will forfeit the license
fee and must wait 6 months to reapply. Please contact your inspector to schedule your next Re-License Inspection.
Regulated activity can continue under your existing USDA license until it expires.
End of report.
